title: fix(openai): Codex login says manual entry is required while browser sign-in still works
body:
Closes #191553
Related: #80963

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex login says it switched to manual entry about 16 seconds in while the browser sign-in is still working, and says it is waiting for the browser when the callback port is unavailable.

## User Impact

User impact: someone taking longer than 16 seconds to sign in sees `Still waiting for the browser. Finish signing in there, or paste the redirect URL below.` If the browser finishes after that, the terminal confirms `OpenAI OAuth complete`.

When the callback port cannot be used, the login no longer waits for a callback that cannot arrive. It asks straight away and says why: `OpenClaw could not use localhost:1455, so the browser cannot finish sign-in here. Sign in there, then paste the redirect URL from its address bar below.`

When the callback is listening, the flow, its 16-second timing and the paste prompt stay the same, and only the messages differ.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser callback keeps racing the paste prompt, so the prompt is an extra way to finish, not a change of mode. The timer stays because the prompt is the way out when a callback can never arrive. The misleading `callback_timeout` log line is removed. A completion line is added because the progress line has already ended by the time the prompt opens.

The login already learns when its callback server fails to bind. That result goes to the local fallback, so the wording follows what happened and no separate port check is needed. Any bind failure takes this path, so the message says `could not use` instead of assuming another process holds the port.

## Evidence

**Successful live login — November 5, 2026:** At head `6d279b834d6acea1018ffd4f28eae6bd2e98c1cf`, `pnpm openclaw models auth login --provider openai --method oauth --force` completed with patched Node 24.22.1 and isolated config/state after a frozen-lockfile install and successful runtime build. I waited for the delayed paste offer, then completed real browser authorization without entering anything at the paste prompt. The prompt stopped accepting input, `OpenAI OAuth complete` rendered on its own line, the OAuth profile was saved, and the CLI exited 0. The callback listener closed afterward. This supersedes the earlier real-sign-in and completion-rendering limitations below. No Gateway was running for the isolated state, so its refresh warning is not Gateway-login proof.

Redacted terminal capture: `pr191554-login-redacted.log`, lines 31–47:

```text
31  ◇  Still waiting for the browser. Finish signing in there, or paste the redirect URL below.
33  ◆  Paste the authorization code (or full redirect URL):
38  OpenAI OAuth complete
39  Updated config: [isolated scratch]/state/openclaw.json
41  Warning: Model auth changes were saved, but the local Gateway could not refresh them. Run `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the saved changes.
42  Auth profile: openai:[account redacted] (openai/oauth)
47  Script done on 2026-11-05 11:38:13-05:00 [COMMAND_EXIT_CODE="0"]
```

Live Linux CLI runs at `6d279b834d6acea1018ffd4f28eae6bd2e98c1cf`, using patched Node 24.22.1 and `pnpm openclaw models auth login --provider openai --method oauth`:

- **Late browser:** the CLI displayed `Still waiting for the browser. Finish signing in there, or paste the redirect URL below.` and the paste prompt. The callback TCP listener on localhost:1455 remained open after the message.
- **Occupied port:** a test-owned listener held `::1:1455`. The CLI displayed the unavailable-port message and the paste prompt.
- Both runs selected local-browser mode. No desktop opener was installed, no credentials were entered, and no callback was submitted. Both were deliberately interrupted after the requested behavior was observed; the launcher reported exit 137. Neither run completed a sign-in or exercised the `OpenAI OAuth complete` line.

Live in a clean macOS VM:

- At the offer, the terminal showed the new `Still waiting for the browser` line and the paste prompt.
- A callback sent 2 seconds later was answered with HTTP 200, and the login moved on to OpenAI's token exchange.
- The callback used a made-up code, so OpenAI's HTTP 401 was the expected result.

Unpatched 2026.10.9 gave the same callback and exchange result under the `Manual OAuth entry required` wording. That shows the listening case changes words, not behavior.

Tests: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts` passes 40 of 40, including a test that holds port 1455 with a real listener. Without the wording change, 1 of 39 fails; without the unavailable-port change, 1 of 40 fails. `src/plugins/provider-openai-chatgpt-oauth.test.ts` passes 4 of 4, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/error-text.test.ts` passes 11 of 11 on the wording commit.

Not tested:

- A real sign-in, so `OpenAI OAuth complete` after a live browser finish is covered by the unit test only.
- Whether the confirmation line renders cleanly as the prompt closes, for the same reason.
- Login through a running Gateway. That path failed in the test overlay, so it was not exercised.
- Remote and VPS login, which this change does not touch. With the port unavailable there, the note saying sign-in may finish automatically stays wrong.
- A real browser navigating to the occupied callback port. The Linux CLI run verified the unavailable-port message with a real listener; what the browser shows depends on what holds the port.
- Windows.
- A packaged release artifact from this branch. The macOS live run overlaid a runtime-only build on the 2026.10.9 package, with some dependencies added by hand. The Linux runs used the source CLI at `6d279b8`.
- Typecheck was not run locally, and `oxlint` crashed on the linked dependencies used for local testing. Hosted checks on `6d279b8` have no failing or pending checks; `control-ui-performance` was skipped. ClawSweeper's review covers `e6ab318`; the unused progress updater it identified is removed, and a review of `6d279b8` is still needed.

The UI build reported Chat boot JS at 1251.0 KiB against a 1250.0 KiB cap and total CSS at 312.1 KiB against 302.1 KiB. Main also exceeds both absolute budgets: [its hosted build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41786317865/job/126429542049) reports 1,282,424 B Chat boot JS and 323,023 B total CSS, both above that run's caps. This PR changes only OAuth runtime and test files, with no UI build-input changes. The warnings reflect budget excess also present on main; no paired candidate/base build was run to measure an exact byte delta for this PR.

#80971 proposed a port check before opening the browser and was closed unmerged. This change still opens the browser, because the address bar is where the redirect URL comes from.
